introduction: “This Wine of unity hath another Wine-Giver, and its intoxication another quality. That diminisheth consciousness, while this increaseth it.” A religion that forbids alcohol speaks constantly of wine: the “choice sealed Wine” of revelation whose seal is now broken, the cup of the Covenant, Jamshíd’s goblet, the tavern of the divine love. This guide collects that language and its explanations. The Qur’an gave the phrase “a pure wine, sealed” and the rivers of wine in Paradise while forbidding strong drink on earth; the Bible has the cup that runs over, the cup of salvation, “thy love is better than wine”, the new wine and the wine of Cana, and “be not drunk with wine … but be filled with the Spirit”. Persian poetry is the nearer source, and FitzGerald’s Khayyám shows how ambiguous its cup can be. The Psalmist’s gladdening wine, Ben Sira’s praise of it and Seneca’s contempt for drunkenness set off what the readings do with the image.
questions: Reading 1 says this wine increases consciousness. List the ways the readings contrast the two wines. What experience are they pointing to?
Why would scriptures that forbid drinking use wine as their chief image for the love of God?
In Khayyám and much Persian verse it is unclear whether the wine is literal. Does that ambiguity enrich the poetry or make it dangerous? How do the readings remove it?
Jesus speaks of a cup of suffering. Readings 97 and 99 join intoxication with tests. Is the wine of the Covenant sweet or bitter?
Reading 61 calls the laws of God “the choice Wine”. How can a commandment be an intoxication?
What in ordinary sober life corresponds to what these readings call being drunk?

outside.why: A wine that increases consciousness where the other diminishes it. Be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.
The first Christians were taken for drunkards at Pentecost: these men are full of new wine. Peter answered that it was only the third hour of the day.
The cup gives a passing delight; this wine does not fade. Thy love is better than wine.
The wine of the vineyard yields a moment’s pleasure. At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.

Some are drunk and joyous from the wine of grapes. The Psalmist counts it among God’s gifts: wine that maketh glad the heart of man. And Ben Sira: wine is as good as life to a man, if it be drunk moderately. The readings forbid the drink and keep the image. Why does the image survive the prohibition?
Drink of this wine as much as thou canst. O taste and see that the Lord is good.

“This wine is spirit-giving, not hangover-inducing.” Omar Khayyám, in FitzGerald’s English, is the poet of the other wine, or seems to be: readers have never agreed whether his cup is the tavern’s or the mystic’s. Persian poetry gave the Bahá’í writings this vocabulary. How does one tell which wine a poem means?
“Deliver them from intoxicating drinks.” The Qur’an: strong drink and games of chance are only an infamy of Satan’s handiwork. Leave it aside.
Cassio, sober again: O God, that men should put an enemy in their mouths to steal away their brains!
“Take thou a cup of My choice-sealed wine.” The phrase is the Qur’an’s, of the drink of the righteous in Paradise: they are given to drink of a pure wine, sealed.
Crystal goblets in the hand of the Cupbearer of eternity. Thou preparest a table before me; my cup runneth over.
Jamshíd’s world-reflecting cup. FitzGerald’s Omar on the same king: the courts where Jamshýd gloried and drank deep are kept by the lion and the lizard.
The cup of the Covenant goes round. He took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; for this is my blood of the new testament.
The cup in the form of the Word. I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord.
The seal of the choice Wine has been broken in this Day. Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break; but they put new wine into new bottles.
Luke adds a wry observation: no man having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better. Why is new wine hard to accept?
A wine sealed from eternity and now opened. At Cana the governor of the feast said: thou hast kept the good wine until now.
“Approach, and quaff your fill.” Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
A chalice of the Kawthar of immortality. The Garden promised to the righteous has rivers of water, of milk, and rivers of wine delicious to the drinkers.
“Observe My commandments, for the love of My beauty”: the laws themselves as the choice wine. The judgments of the Lord are sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.
He relieved us of every heavy load. My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
The one wine forbidden and the other commanded. Wine and new wine take away the heart.

This nectar is not for every soul, only for the enduring. Jesus asked two disciples: can ye drink of the cup that I drink of? The cup there is suffering. Is the wine of these readings ever that cup? See 97 and 99.
Whoever has drunk of this wine has attained eternal life. He that believeth on me shall never thirst.
Falling and rising in Thy path, intoxicated with the wine of the Covenant. O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.
Nothing can quench this thirst but Thy presence. My soul thirsteth for thee in a dry and thirsty land.
Make me happy by the wine of Thy love. He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
Free me from these chains. Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free.
Every wine’s intoxication ends in a hangover and every joy in weariness, except this. Keats: in the very temple of Delight veil’d Melancholy has her sovran shrine.
Blessed is he who has attained the days of God and drunk. I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.
This wine “increaseth awareness”. It is high time to awake out of sleep.
Be happy and joyous. The joy of the Lord is your strength.
The table of love is spread and the banquet of knowledge is ready. A certain man made a great supper, and bade many: come; for all things are now ready.
In a world of upheaval, one cup. Tagore: thou ever pourest for me the fresh draught of thy wine of various colours and fragrance, filling this earthen vessel to the brim.
The goblet overflows and the decanter weeps with joy. Rumi’s poem begins in the lover’s other mood: hearken to the reed-flute, how it complains, lamenting its banishment from its home.
Act so that others become intoxicated with this wine. Let your light so shine before men.

The divine who has drunk the holy Wine is “as an eye unto the world”. Seneca judged drunkenness coldly: nothing but a condition of insanity purposely assumed. Mystics of every tradition have nonetheless described their highest state as intoxication. What does the figure say that sober language cannot?

shortfall: Seven of the ten stretches are short salutations and blessings (“thou hast drunk the wine of …”, “blessed is he who hath quaffed …”) that differ only in the name of the wine; companions were given to the distinct ideas, and more than half the readings were left without.
